name: ops-advisor
description: A prioritised recommendations report on the estate in the ops inventory, with evidence: reliability (missing monitoring and dashboards, single points of failure from the dependency graph, anomalies, noisy alerts, SLOs), capacity (trends and forecasts), security posture (ports, ssh, packages, certificates, root containers, secrets in env) and cost (idle and oversized resources) - each analysed in parallel by its specialist, then merged into .harness/ops/reports/ops-advisor.md. Read-only: it changes nothing (on hosts it works as their read-only account).

estate.description: a short description of the estate: hosts, services, monitoring

survey.title: Survey the estate

reliability.title: Reliability
reliability.prompt:
Estate: {{state.estate}}
Analyse RELIABILITY, read-only, and write .harness/ops/reports/advisor/reliability.md: services in the inventory with no health URL, no metrics job or no alert rule (missing monitoring), Prometheus targets that are down, containers without a health check or restart policy, single points of failure (one instance, one host, no backup), noisy or always-firing alerts (ops_check action history), SLOs without alerts and their burn (slo_status), restart loops and OOM kills.
With the tools this session has: topology spof (single points of failure from the dependency graph: one instance, a host running several services, a node whose loss disconnects others - with what depends on each); grafana coverage and grafana alerts (services with no dashboard or no Grafana alert rule, rules that are firing or erroring); anomalies for each service with a metrics job (window 6h, history 7d: signals unusual against the same hours on earlier days - a finding only when strong or sustained).
Every recommendation in the format: Title, Priority (P1-P4), Finding, Evidence (the exact query or command, the numbers, and the evidence id [ev-...]; dashboard links where there are), Impact, Effort (S/M/L), Change (the exact change), Risk.

Report: the recommendations' titles with priorities.

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.prompt:
Estate: {{state.estate}}
Analyse CAPACITY, read-only, and write .harness/ops/reports/advisor/capacity.md: for CPU, memory and every filesystem (node-exporter metrics where scraped; host_stats otherwise), and request rates of the services, use capacity_forecast (range 7d or what data exists) to give trends, time to full and headroom. Say plainly when the data is too short to forecast. Where the session has the anomalies tool, check the request rates against earlier days (window 1d, period 1w when there is the history) to tell growth from a one-off.
Every recommendation in the format: Title, Priority, Finding, Evidence, Impact, Effort, Change, Risk.

Report: the recommendations' titles with priorities.

security.title: Security posture
security.prompt:
Estate: {{state.estate}}
Analyse SECURITY POSTURE with read-only checks only, and write .harness/ops/reports/advisor/security.md: TLS certificates of every service with a TLS endpoint (probe type tls: expired, expiring, self-signed, name mismatch), containers running as root or privileged and secret-looking environment variables (docker_status - names only, never values), and on hosts reachable over ssh: listening ports (ss -tlnp), sshd settings (sshd -T: PasswordAuthentication, PermitRootLogin; or the config file where the reader cannot run it), outdated packages. ssh_exec runs as the host's read-only account by default - use only that; never as: "operator" (this workflow changes nothing).
Every recommendation in the format: Title, Priority, Finding, Evidence, Impact, Effort, Change, Risk.

Report: the recommendations' titles with priorities.

cost.title: Cost
cost.prompt:
Estate: {{state.estate}}
Analyse COST, read-only, and write .harness/ops/reports/advisor/cost.md: idle or oversized containers and hosts (CPU and memory use against limits and capacity over the data available), stopped containers and unused resources, duplicated services.
Every recommendation in the format: Title, Priority, Finding, Evidence, Impact, Effort, Change, Risk.

Report: the recommendations' titles with priorities.
